proof_summary: For each \(k\ge 60\), set \(n=2k+1\); every nonzero matrix entry supplies two primes whose sum is \(2n=4k+2\), so if no such prime pair existed the entire matrix—and hence its determinant—would be zero, contradicting the assumed nonvanishing. The finitely many cases \(1\le k<60\) are handled by explicit prime decompositions.
